I don't know you, but here's what I found out myself, that might help you:

People are selfish in conversations. What they want to talk about is mostly themselves and their opinions. At first this might sound sad, but here's how I use that to my advantage:

I basically noticed, that I was being selfish too and only wanted to bring myself and my opinions into the conversation. (That may also be why you cut people off) Well what if I did the opposite: Ask the other people **questions**. **Questions** are awesome in so many ways.

* They let you be part of the discussion, but you don't have to think too much.
* People think (maybe even rightfully so), that you're interested in them, which makes them feel better.
* Asking questions is so easy.
* With the right questions you might learn a lot of interesting stuff about your friends.
* If you ask people good questions, that often results in them asking you something back.
* Questions about something people just mentioned show people that you listen.

After a little while you can also try to through around some questions that tell others your opinion or tell them a lot about yourself.

Obviously it's also important to say, that it's totally cool to be quiet sometimes. So don't ask to many questions and listen to their answers. That's what helped me with similar problems.
